note: PROVISIONAL model-drafted highlight gold, pending human adjudication. May SCREEN hypotheses in the fast loop only; keep/discard decisions must cite human-signed gold (ADR 0042).

spans.text: A few very bright particles or fragments or something that go drifting by as we maneuver.
spans.why: crew's initial report of bright drifting particles

spans.text: There's a whole bunch of big ones on my window there.
Looks like the 4th of July out Ron's window.
They're very jagged, angular, fragmented or tumbling.
spans.why: key shape description: jagged, angular, fragmented, tumbling

spans.text: They look like pieces or something.
spans.why: crew rejects Ground's 'fluid' reading - they are pieces

spans.text: these fragments are not, are tumbling at a very slow rate.
I got the impression maybe they were curved a little bit, as if they might be off the side of the S-4B.
spans.why: crew hypothesis: the fragments may have come off the S-IVB stage

spans.text: Maybe there's paint coming off of it.
one of the flags, I thought it was in the S-2, but it might be on the S-4.
spans.why: Ground control's peeling-flag hypothesis for the fragments

spans.text: with the maneuver complete, the fragment field is essentially static, except for very slight tumbling within the fragment.
spans.why: the fragment field is static after the S-IVB maneuver

spans.text: Every once in a while a fragment of considerably higher velocity than the others goes across my window, but that's very rare.
there's no apparent relative motion between fragments.
they are flat, flake-like particles, some maybe six inches across
spans.why: Cernan: flat, flake-like particles about six inches across

spans.text: most of them seem to be twinkling, and I think for the most part they're all moving away from us
spans.why: Cernan: the particles twinkle and move away from the spacecraft
